lesson_title: One Bin Bag, Seven Second Lives
hook_text: Your rubbish bag is a mixture. Sort it, and almost everything in it gets a second life.
clip_script: Open a bin bag: food scraps, a cooldrink bottle, a tin can, newspaper, a glass jar, a battery. Mixed together, it all gets buried in a landfill that leaks and smells. Sorted, it becomes a resource. At a recycling plant, hands pull out big items, giant sieves sort sizes, magnets snatch the steel can, a spinning magnet flicks out the aluminium, fans blow paper away, and cameras spot the plastic. The can melts into new metal, forever. The jar becomes a new jar, forever. The newspaper becomes new paper, but only a few times, because its fibres get shorter. The bottle can become pillow stuffing. Food scraps become compost. And the battery? Never in the bin: it goes to a drop-off point. But the best rubbish of all is the rubbish you never make.
visual_style: Whiteboard bin bag spilling its contents onto a conveyor belt; each item peeling off to its machine and transforming; a battery walking to a drop-off box; a final waste-hierarchy ladder.
pacing: Quick sort-line montage, rapid transformations, a thoughtful last line.
